data.claim: A knob [harness].suspended (default glm) consulted at the four write points (setup/adopt/onboard selection, companion register, docs refresh, upgrade MCP apply) is sufficient for an adopt of every known agent to write no .zcode/config.json, while the descriptor stays loadable and resume is one config line.
data.falsifier: A temp-repo adopt with default config that still creates .zcode/config.json, or a resume (suspended = []) that does not restore the write.
data.mechanism: Every writer reaches glm through AGENT_TARGETS keys handed in by api/setup/adopt.setup (default list(AGENT_TARGETS)), by companions.register(agent), by refresh_docs over the deltas on disk, or by upgrade _apply_mcp; filtering those by the config set leaves the descriptor registry untouched.
data.probe_output: Before the change (same tests, unfixed code): 8 failed 5 passed in tests/test_harness_suspended.py, first failure assert not (repo / '.zcode/config.json').exists() -> AssertionError: assert not True. After: uv run pytest tests/test_harness_suspended.py -q -> 15 passed.
data.question: Where must a suspension be enforced so no ZCode file is written?

chunk_findings.detail: With the default configuration, `ddflow harness list` renders a suspended harness as `... SUSPENDED: resume with ...`, but it omits the reason required by the design. For example, running `harness_list` on a default temp repo prints a `glm` row with a resume command, but not the intended explanation such as “ZCode support is suspended: nothing is installed or updated.” The reason is only surfaced by `harness_show` via `HS.note`, so a user relying on `harness list` sees the status and resume hint without the stated reason.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness.py:harness_list

chunk_findings.detail: `_without_suspended` filters every requested id against `[harness].suspended` before the caller computes `unknown`, so an id that is listed as suspended but is not a known harness is silently dropped. For example, if the config contains `[harness].suspended = ["glmm"]` (typo, or a removed descriptor) and the user runs `ddflow onboard harness --accept glmm`, `want` becomes `[]` and `paused` is also `[]` because `HR.get("glmm")` is `None`; the function then returns the `nothing` outcome “no agent adopted here: name one with --accept <id>” instead of the `failed` unknown-harness outcome. This hides an unknown/invalid suspended harness id and gives the user a misleading “no agent” message even though one was named.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/onboard.py:_without_suspended

chunk_findings.detail: With the default suspended list, `ddflow adopt --agents glm` makes `_suspension` return `agents=[]` and a suspended note, so the new `if asked and not agents` branch calls `_nothing_to_adopt`. That function renders the outcome with `human.render(out)`, but the visible code in this file renders setup outcomes with `_human.render(out)` and the diff adds no `human` import or definition. The exact acceptance path for “naming a suspended agent writes nothing and exits zero” therefore hits an undefined/non-renderer `human` name and crashes (or at least bypasses the configured `_human` renderer) instead of returning the required suspended note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/adopt.py:_nothing_to_adopt

chunk_findings.detail: `split()` accepts an arbitrary `Iterable`, but it iterates `agents` twice: once to build `active` and again to build `suspended`. If a caller passes a generator or any single-pass iterable, the first comprehension exhausts it and the second returns `[]`. For example, `split((a for a in ["glm", "claude"]), cfg)` returns `(["claude"], [])`, so the suspended harness is silently dropped from the suspended list. If adopt/onboard uses this to decide which notes to show, it can omit the “ZCode is suspended” note even though the harness was requested.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harness_suspend.py:split

chunk_findings.detail: `existing_files()` treats any file at a suspended harness’s MCP path as “written by an earlier adopt,” but it only checks `(repo / h.mcp.path).is_file()`. With the default suspended `glm`, a repository that already contains a user-created `.zcode/config.json` (or one created by ZCode itself) will cause `doctor_notes()` to report `glm: .zcode/config.json was written by an earlier adopt and is left as it is...`. That is wrong because the code has no evidence ddflow wrote the file, and it may lead users to delete a config they intentionally created.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harness_suspend.py:existing_files

chunk_findings.detail: The suspension guard checks only whether *all* targets for a config path are suspended, then unconditionally registers `keys[0]`. If an upgrade fragment targets a `rel` that matches more than one agent target (the code explicitly supports this by building `keys`), default `[harness].suspended = ["glm"]`, and `glm` is the first matching key while another unsuspended target also matches, the `all(...)` test is false and `AD._register_mcp(repo, keys[0])` is called for the suspended `glm` target. That writes/updates the ZCode MCP entry despite suspension, violating the “never written to” rule for suspended harnesses [D-zcode-support-suspended-2026-11-14].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply/_appliers.py:196-198

chunk_findings.detail: The added blockquote is an unconditional statement in a driver delta note that is loaded when the `glm` harness is active. It says support is suspended and “nothing below is installed or updated for it.” If a user resumes `glm` by removing it from `[harness].suspended` (or running the suggested resume command), adopting or driving `glm` still reads this same template and is told the harness is suspended and its delta instructions should be ignored. That contradicts the intended “resume is one config line” behavior: after resume, the old driver delta note should be used, not a note claiming the harness is inactive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/zcode-glm.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: The new suspended-agent pin is parametrized from `Config().harness.suspended`, i.e. the effective user/repo config, not the default under test. If a developer or CI environment has `[harness].suspended = []` (for example after running `ddflow harness resume glm` in their user config), `SUSPENDED` is empty, so `test_adopt_writes_nothing_for_a_suspended_agent` is collected with no cases and the required “adopt of a suspended agent writes no `.zcode/config.json`” check silently disappears while the suite still passes. Conversely, if the effective config suspends a harness that has no MCP file (`target.config is None`), the same test fails on `assert target.config` even though the default `glm` suspension is unchanged. The test should pin the default suspended id or explicitly isolate/override config rather than trusting ambient config.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adopt.py:SUSPENDED

chunk_findings.detail: The test is meant to prove that suspension/resume works for a non-default harness, but it only checks the config list and the absence of `mcp.json` before resume. It never asserts the required suspension note, and after resume it never runs `ddflow adopt --agents qodo` to prove adoption is restored. A concrete false-positive is possible: if `adopt` contains a hard skip for `qodo` and `harness suspend`/`resume` merely edit the TOML list, the test still passes—`adopt --agents qodo` writes no `mcp.json` before resume, `_suspended_in(repo)` becomes `["glm"]` after resume, and no assertion fails—while `qodo` remains effectively suspended and no clear note is printed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_suspended.py:test_suspend_then_resume_another_harness

chunk_findings.detail: `test_roborev_findings.py` line 257 modifies `test_roborev_findings_all_agents_register` to resume the `glm` harness (`run_cli(repo, "harness", "resume", "glm")`) before looping over `("vscode", "copilot", "claude", "opencode", "glm")`. However, the P-zcode tasks including `ZC-driver`, `ZC-hooks`, `ZC-identity`, `ZC-skills-commands`, and `ZC-parity` are stated in the intent to be BLOCKED and the `glm` harness code is not yet of good quality, meaning resuming `glm` in tests and expecting it to succeed contradicts the core safety intent of suspending ZCode due to poor quality. Furthermore, the intent states: "A suspended harness is: [...] still loadable by name, so an existing adoption does not crash", but invoking `harness resume glm` on an incomplete harness violates the review instructions and safety-by-default design rules (`r-safe-by-default`, `r-upgrade-safe`) by enabling a known bad harness in the test suite without verifying its underlying driver implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py:257

chunk_findings.detail: With the default configuration, `ddflow harness list` emits only `SUSPENDED: resume with \`...\`` for the suspended harness. The change’s design requires the list entry to include both the reason and the one-line resume, and the reason/note is available via `HS.note` (used in `harness_show`), but `harness_list` never includes it. Thus a user running `ddflow harness list` sees that `glm` is suspended and how to resume it, but not the required reason that ZCode support is suspended and nothing is installed or updated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness.py:harness_list

chunk_findings.detail: The new no-op path renders the outcome with `human.render(out)`, while the existing code in the same file renders with `_human.render(out)` (see the unchanged refresh-docs branch in this hunk). With the module's existing `_human` alias, `human` is not defined, so `ddflow setup --agents glm` under the default `[harness].suspended = ["glm"]` reaches `_nothing_to_adopt` and raises `NameError: name 'human' is not defined` instead of exiting successfully with the suspended note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/adopt.py:_nothing_to_adopt

chunk_findings.detail: `split` iterates its `agents` argument twice. If a caller passes a generator or other one-shot iterator, the first list comprehension exhausts it and the second comprehension sees nothing, so suspended agents are silently dropped from the returned `suspended` list. For example, with the default config, `split((a for a in ["claude", "glm"]), cfg)` returns `(["claude"], [])` instead of `(["claude"], ["glm"])`, so callers relying on the suspended list to suppress writes or print notes will miss `glm`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harness_suspend.py:split

chunk_findings.detail: This function treats the mere existence of a suspended harness’s MCP path as proof that ddflow previously wrote the file. In a fresh repository where the user manually created `.zcode/config.json` (or another tool created it), with the default suspended set containing `glm`, `doctor_notes(repo, cfg)` returns a note saying `glm: .zcode/config.json was written by an earlier adopt...` even though ddflow never wrote it. The intent requires doctor to note only a ddflow-written file; this false attribution can mislead the user into deleting their own config file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harness_suspend.py:existing_files

chunk_findings.detail: The new suspension guard skips only when *every* key that writes the same MCP config is suspended, but the code then registers `keys[0]`. If `AD.AGENT_TARGETS` contains more than one key for the same `rel` (e.g. an alias or a harness added via `ddflow harness add` that uses the same MCP path as a suspended harness), and the first key is suspended while another is not, `all(k in off for k in keys)` is false, so execution falls through to `AD._register_mcp(repo, keys[0])` and writes/updates the MCP config for the suspended harness anyway. For example, with `[harness].suspended = ["glm"]` and `keys == ["glm", "glm2"]` for `.zcode/config.json`, the suspended `glm` entry is still installed, violating the “never written to” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply/_appliers.py:196

chunk_findings.detail: The added `SUSPENDED` block is written unconditionally into the source delta note that is copied into a user’s driver when ZCode is adopted. The intent and this note itself define resume as removing `glm` from `[harness].suspended` (one config line / `ddflow harness resume glm`). After a user resumes ZCode and runs `ddflow adopt glm` (or adopts all agents), the installed delta note will still begin with “SUSPENDED … nothing below is installed or updated for it”, which is false for an active harness and can instruct the driver/agent to skip ZCode-specific installation. Thus removing the config entry does not restore the old delta-note behaviour; it requires manually editing this template, contradicting the reversibility/acceptance requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/zcode-glm.md:3-7

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named “writes nothing” and the intent says a suspended harness must not receive “no .zcode/config.json, no AGENTS.md row, no hooks,” but the test only asserts that `.zcode` does not exist. If a regression suppresses the `.zcode/config.json` writer while still appending a `glm` row to `AGENTS.md` (or writing hooks), `run_cli(repo, "adopt", "--agents", "glm")` can still exit 0, emit the suspension note, and pass this test. Thus the test gives false assurance for a suspended harness that is still partially written to.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_suspended.py:test_naming_the_suspended_agent_writes_nothing_and_exits_zero

The change’s design requires the list entry to include both the reason and the one-line resume, and the reason/note is available via `HS.note` (used in `harness_show`), but `harness_list` never includes it. Thus a user running `ddflow harness list` sees that `glm` is suspended and how to resume it, but not the required reason that ZCode support is suspended and nothing is installed or updated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness.py:harness_list

chunk_findings.detail: The new no-op path renders the outcome with `human.render(out)`, while the existing code in the same file renders with `_human.render(out)` (see the unchanged refresh-docs branch in this hunk). With the module's existing `_human` alias, `human` is not defined, so `ddflow setup --agents glm` under the default `[harness].suspended = ["glm"]` reaches `_nothing_to_adopt` and raises `NameError: name 'human' is not defined` instead of exiting successfully with the suspended note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/adopt.py:_nothing_to_adopt

chunk_findings.detail: `split` iterates its `agents` argument twice. If a caller passes a generator or other one-shot iterator, the first list comprehension exhausts it and the second comprehension sees nothing, so suspended agents are silently dropped from the returned `suspended` list. For example, with the default config, `split((a for a in ["claude", "glm"]), cfg)` returns `(["claude"], [])` instead of `(["claude"], ["glm"])`, so callers relying on the suspended list to suppress writes or print notes will miss `glm`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harness_suspend.py:split

chunk_findings.detail: This function treats the mere existence of a suspended harness’s MCP path as proof that ddflow previously wrote the file. In a fresh repository where the user manually created `.zcode/config.json` (or another tool created it), with the default suspended set containing `glm`, `doctor_notes(repo, cfg)` returns a note saying `glm: .zcode/config.json was written by an earlier adopt...` even though ddflow never wrote it. The intent requires doctor to note only a ddflow-written file; this false attribution can mislead the user into deleting their own config file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harness_suspend.py:existing_files

chunk_findings.detail: The new suspension guard skips only when *every* key that writes the same MCP config is suspended, but the code then registers `keys[0]`. If `AD.AGENT_TARGETS` contains more than one key for the same `rel` (e.g. an alias or a harness added via `ddflow harness add` that uses the same MCP path as a suspended harness), and the first key is suspended while another is not, `all(k in off for k in keys)` is false, so execution falls through to `AD._register_mcp(repo, keys[0])` and writes/updates the MCP config for the suspended harness anyway. For example, with `[harness].suspended = ["glm"]` and `keys == ["glm", "glm2"]` for `.zcode/config.json`, the suspended `glm` entry is still installed, violating the “never written to” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_apply/_appliers.py:196

chunk_findings.detail: The added `SUSPENDED` block is written unconditionally into the source delta note that is copied into a user’s driver when ZCode is adopted. The intent and this note itself define resume as removing `glm` from `[harness].suspended` (one config line / `ddflow harness resume glm`). After a user resumes ZCode and runs `ddflow adopt glm` (or adopts all agents), the installed delta note will still begin with “SUSPENDED … nothing below is installed or updated for it”, which is false for an active harness and can instruct the driver/agent to skip ZCode-specific installation. Thus removing the config entry does not restore the old delta-note behaviour; it requires manually editing this template, contradicting the reversibility/acceptance requirement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/zcode-glm.md:3-7

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named “writes nothing” and the intent says a suspended harness must not receive “no .zcode/config.json, no AGENTS.md row, no hooks,” but the test only asserts that `.zcode` does not exist. If a regression suppresses the `.zcode/config.json` writer while still appending a `glm` row to `AGENTS.md` (or writing hooks), `run_cli(repo, "adopt", "--agents", "glm")` can still exit 0, emit the suspension note, and pass this test. Thus the test gives false assurance for a suspended harness that is still partially written to.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_suspended.py:test_naming_the_suspended_agent_writes_nothing_and_exits_zero

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten banner still hard-codes a suspension notice in the source delta note that is copied into a ZCode driver when the harness is active. After an operator resumes ZCode (`ddflow harness resume glm` / removing `glm` from `[harness].suspended`) and then runs `ddflow adopt --agents glm`, the installed delta note still begins with the block quote `> **SUSPENDED while ...**` and still contains “nothing below is installed or updated for it.” The new sentence “once resumed … this banner no longer does” is not enforced by conditional rendering or note rewriting; an agent reading the resumed driver still sees a `SUSPENDED` banner and may skip the instructions below it. This is a new defect introduced by the new claim that the banner no longer applies, because the static note remains unchanged after resume.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/zcode-glm.md:3-7

chunk_findings.detail: `test_roborev_findings.py` line 257 modifies `test_roborev_findings_all_agents_register` to resume the `glm` harness (`run_cli(repo, "harness", "resume", "glm")`) before looping over `("vscode", "copilot", "claude", "opencode", "glm")`. However, the P-zcode tasks including `ZC-driver`, `ZC-hooks`, `ZC-identity`, `ZC-skills-commands`, and `ZC-parity` are stated in the intent to be BLOCKED and the `glm` harness code is not yet of good quality, meaning resuming `glm` in tests and expecting it to succeed contradicts the core safety intent of suspending ZCode due to poor quality. Furthermore, the intent states: "A suspended harness is: [...] still loadable by name, so an existing adoption does not crash", but invoking `harness resume glm` on an incomplete harness violates the review instructions and safety-by-default design rules (`r-safe-by-default`, `r-upgrade-safe`) by enabling a known bad harness in the test suite without verifying its underlying driver implementation.
